haiku-low.q1: Held 10 minutes (expires_at = now + 10 min). If unclaimed, a per-minute timer marks it EXPIRED and returns stock to sale.
haiku-low.q2: Reserved before charging. If any line is short, nothing is reserved, the order is cancelled with the short items shown, and no payment is requested.
haiku-low.q3: Charge uses the order id as idempotency key; retries reuse it, so the provider cannot charge twice. One order has at most one charge.
haiku-low.q4: Order is set CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK and emails the customer. Payment records a full REFUND_PENDING refund and calls the provider, which is retried until accepted.
haiku-low.q5: Emptied only when OrderConfirmed arrives with a matching saved order id. On any failure the cart is left unchanged for another Place order.
haiku-low.q6: Events between services drive each step. Order moves the order through its statuses, and the stored order status records how far each checkout has got.
haiku-low.q7: The provider sends a webhook to Payment, which publishes PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined over the broker to Order.
haiku-low.q8: Payment checks the provider event id against processed events; duplicates get 200 OK and nothing else. All consumers also record handled event ids.
haiku-low.q9: Order sets CANCELLED_PAYMENT_DECLINED and publishes OrderCancelled. Inventory releases the hold straight away if still HELD, otherwise does nothing.
haiku-low.q10: Inventory retries claiming all lines once. If every line is still free, it fulfils; if not, StockClaimFailed triggers a refund.
haiku-low.q11: It stays REFUND_PENDING in Payment's database. A retry timer resends with backoff, never giving up; after 5 failures operations is alerted.
haiku-low.q12: Cart service empties the cart when it consumes OrderConfirmed, only if the order id matches the one it saved.

sonnet.q1: Held 10 minutes (expires_at = now + 10 min). If not claimed in time, the Inventory timer (runs every minute) marks it EXPIRED and stock goes back on sale; a late claim can still retake the lines if all are still free.
sonnet.q2: Reserved before the charge (payment is requested only after StockReserved). If any line is short, nothing is reserved (all-or-nothing); StockRejected with the short items is sent, order becomes CANCELLED_SHORT_STOCK, and no payment is requested.
sonnet.q3: The charge uses the order id as idempotency key, and retries reuse it, so the provider cannot charge twice; one order has at most one charge.
sonnet.q4: Order becomes CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK, emails the customer (cancelled, full refund coming), and publishes RefundRequested. Payment saves a REFUND_PENDING for the full amount, calls the provider refund, then marks REFUNDED. Nothing ships.
sonnet.q5: The cart is emptied only on the OrderConfirmed event (Cart empties it if the order id matches the saved one). On any failure (short stock, declined, out of stock) the cart is left unchanged so the customer can retry.
sonnet.q6: Events over the shared message broker (via each service's transactional outbox and relay) move it between services. The record of progress is the order status in the Order service (plus its refund status).
sonnet.q7: The provider sends a webhook to Payment, which verifies it, records it and publishes PaymentSucceeded/PaymentDeclined over the broker to Order, which finishes the order.
sonnet.q8: Webhooks: Payment checks the provider event id against its processed-events table; duplicates get 200 OK and nothing else. The event id and new status are saved in one transaction. Broker events: every consumer records handled event ids, so redeliveries do nothing.
sonnet.q9: Order sets CANCELLED_PAYMENT_DECLINED and publishes OrderCancelled; Inventory then releases the hold immediately if still HELD (stock back on sale). If already expired/released/missing, it does nothing.
sonnet.q10: On ClaimStock with an EXPIRED hold, Inventory tries once to retake all lines all-or-nothing. If every line's available count is at least the quantity, it is CLAIMED and StockClaimed is sent (fulfil). Otherwise StockClaimFailed leads to cancellation and refund. This is a stated design assumption.
sonnet.q11: The refund stays REFUND_PENDING, stored in Payment's database (survives restart). A retry timer re-sends with backoff and never gives up; after 5 failures Payment alerts operations. It leaves pending only by succeeding.
sonnet.q12: The OrderConfirmed event, published by Order after StockClaimed; the Cart service consumes it and empties the cart, only if the order id matches the one it saved.
